headline: Education Ministers of the Turkic States Endorse Permanent TURKUNIB Secretariat and Dedicated Fund for the Orhun Exchange Programme
tags: Ministers of Education, OTS, Orhun Exchange Programme, TURKUNIB Secretariat, quality assurance, academic mobility, Turkistan
paras: The 9th Meeting of the Ministers of Education of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), held on 8 June 2026 in Turkistan, Kazakhstan, delivered some of the most consequential decisions for higher education cooperation in the Turkic world in recent years. The meeting, attended by the Ministers of Education of the OTS Member States and OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev, concluded with the adoption of a joint Communique.

Of particular significance for the university community, the ministers noted that membership of the Turkic Universities Union (TURKUNIB) has grown to 170 universities, and endorsed two landmark institutional steps: the establishment of a Permanent TURKUNIB Secretariat and the creation of a Dedicated Programme Fund for the Orhun Exchange Programme. The OTS has allocated one million US dollars to support the development of the exchange programme, which enables student and staff mobility among universities of the Turkic states.

The ministerial meeting also advanced a broad package of initiatives designed to build a common higher education space across the Turkic world. These include the establishment of a Turkic World Higher Education Data Bank; the creation of a Turkic World Association for Quality Assurance in Higher Education (TWAQA); diploma certification and equivalency mechanisms for TURKUNIB member universities; the establishment of a Turkic Universities League; expanded student and teacher exchange programmes together with a “sister school” practice; a Turkic States Education Information Network; and an Education Cooperation Working Group to carry the agenda forward.

On the margins of the meeting, the OTS Secretary General held bilateral consultations with the Minister of Science and Higher Education of Kazakhstan, Sayasat Nurbek, focusing on the practical steps required to establish the Permanent TURKUNIB Secretariat and the mobility fund, and with the Minister of Science and Education of Azerbaijan, Emin Amrullayev, on cooperation in education, science and academic mobility.

For TURKUNIB and its member universities, the Turkistan decisions represent a decisive step from cooperation to institutionalization. A permanent secretariat, a funded mobility programme, a shared quality assurance framework and recognized diploma equivalency mechanisms together form the backbone of an emerging Turkic World Higher Education Area – an agenda in which TURKUNIB member universities are both the principal contributors and the principal beneficiaries.

headline: TURKUNIB Grows to a Union of More Than 170 Universities: 8th General Assembly in Tashkent Admits 62 New Members and Charts an Institutional Reform Agenda
tags: General Assembly, TURKUNIB, Tashkent International University, membership, Orhun Exchange Programme, higher education
paras: The 8th General Assembly of the Turkic Universities Union (TURKUNIB) convened on 15 October 2025 in Tashkent, hosted by Tashkent International University (TIU) in its capacity as Chair University of the Union for 2025–2026. The Assembly brought together rectors, academics and representatives of more than seventy member universities from across the Turkic world.

The opening session was addressed by senior figures of the Turkic cooperation architecture and of the host country: Hilala Umarova, Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Uzbekistan in charge of educational reform; Kongratbay Sharipov, Minister of Higher Education, Science and Innovation of Uzbekistan; OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev; Shahin Mustafayev, President of the Turkic Academy; and Iskandar Yuldashev, Executive Director of TIU. Recalling that “education has always been a bridge connecting cultures,” the Secretary General underscored the Union's rapid growth: TURKUNIB's membership had reached 109 universities, with a further 62 institutions applying to join.

In its working session, chaired with the participation of OTS Deputy Secretary General Dr. Mirvokhid Azimov, the Assembly adopted a decision admitting all 62 applicant universities – bringing the Union past the 170-member mark – and considered a concept paper on establishing a Permanent TURKUNIB Secretariat together with a dedicated Programme Fund for the Orhun Exchange Programme. Delegates also examined proposals from Türkiye's Council of Higher Education on strengthening the Union's institutional framework, and proposals from the Government of Hungary on a joint Research, Development and Innovation Fund and an enhanced Orhun Exchange Programme.

The Assembly took place against a supportive political backdrop: according to the OTS, the Gabala Declaration adopted at the 12th OTS Summit one week earlier endorsed the reorganization of the Orhun Exchange Programme and the establishment of a Turkic World Higher Education Area, and the OTS announced that it will allocate one million US dollars to support the programme's implementation and expansion.

The Tashkent General Assembly thus marked a turning point for TURKUNIB – the largest enlargement in its history combined with a concrete roadmap toward permanent institutions, secured funding for mobility, and a strengthened role at the centre of higher education cooperation in the Turkic world.

headline: Gabala Summit Places Higher Education at the Heart of the Turkic Agenda: Leaders Endorse Reorganized Orhun Programme and a Turkic World Higher Education Area
tags: OTS Summit, Gabala Declaration, Orhun Exchange Programme, Turkic World Higher Education Area, Heads of State
paras: The 12th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States, held on 7 October 2025 in Gabala, Azerbaijan under the theme “Regional Peace and Security,” produced outcomes of direct and lasting importance for the higher education community of the Turkic world.

The Summit gathered the Presidents of Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Türkiye and Uzbekistan – Ilham Aliyev, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Sadyr Zhaparov, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Shavkat Mirziyoyev – together with Prime Minister of Hungary Viktor Orbán, National Leader of the Turkmen People Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, President of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Ersin Tatar, and OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev. The leaders adopted the Gabala Declaration, established an “OTS+” format for engagement with external partners, and adopted a decision on the development of TURKSOY. Turkmenistan was welcomed as an Observer in the Turkic Academy and the Turkic Culture and Heritage Foundation, and the Chairmanship-in-Office passed from Kyrgyzstan to Azerbaijan.

For universities, the most significant element of the Summit lies in its education provisions. According to the OTS, the Gabala Declaration endorsed the reorganization of the Orhun Exchange Programme and the establishment of a Turkic World Higher Education Area – the two structural reforms around which TURKUNIB's current agenda is built. The Secretary General noted that the Organization now coordinates multilateral cooperation in over forty sectors, “ranging from economic integration and security to education, innovation, and space.”

The Summit's decisions were reflected almost immediately in practice: one week later, the 8th General Assembly of TURKUNIB in Tashkent admitted 62 new member universities and took forward the concept of a Permanent Secretariat and a funded Orhun Exchange Programme.

The Gabala Summit confirmed that higher education, science and innovation are no longer peripheral items on the Turkic cooperation agenda but central pillars of it – providing TURKUNIB and its member universities with a mandate at the highest political level to accelerate the construction of a common higher education space.

headline: Turkic States Leaders Focus on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development at Turkistan Informal Summit
tags: Informal Summit, artificial intelligence, digital development, Turkistan Declaration, Vision-2040, innovation
paras: The Informal Summit of the Organization of Turkic States convened on 15 May 2026 in Turkistan, Kazakhstan, under the theme “Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development” – placing the technologies that are reshaping research, teaching and innovation at the very top of the Turkic cooperation agenda.

Hosted by President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, the Summit brought together President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev, President of the Kyrgyz Republic Sadyr Zhaparov, President of Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev, President of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Tufan Erhürman and OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev.

The leaders adopted the Turkistan Declaration together with decisions on strengthening the institutional and digital capacity of the OTS Secretariat and on the appointment of a Deputy Secretary General. Discussions centred on digital transformation and innovation, artificial intelligence and digital governance, smart infrastructure and innovation ecosystems, and sustainable economic development, framed by the long-term “Turkic World Vision-2040.” The Summit also launched the “Center of Turkic Civilization” initiative – conceived as an international-level multifunctional cultural, scientific and tourist centre integrating the heritage of the Turkic world.

For the academic community, the Turkistan Summit matters well beyond its diplomatic significance. By making artificial intelligence and digital development the unifying theme of the year, the Turkic states have signalled where joint projects, funding priorities and skills initiatives will concentrate – from AI research and digital governance to the innovation ecosystems in which universities play a defining role.

These directions align closely with the mission of TURKUNIB, whose member universities are natural partners in building the region's digital and research capacity. The Summit's emphasis on AI, innovation and a shared scientific infrastructure reinforces the case for deeper inter-university collaboration in precisely the fields the leaders have now identified as strategic.

headline: OTS Moves to Strengthen the Institutional Foundations of the Orhun Exchange Programme and TURKUNIB
tags: Orhun Exchange Programme, TURKUNIB, OTS Secretariat, institutional development, higher education mobility
paras: In January 2026, the Organization of Turkic States took a concrete step toward the professionalization of the Turkic world's flagship academic mobility architecture, announcing the recruitment of dedicated experts for the institutional development of the Orhun Exchange Programme and the Turkic Universities Union (TURKUNIB).

Under the call published on 23 January 2026, the OTS Secretariat sought two consultants to be based at its headquarters in Istanbul: a Legal and Institutional Framework Expert and a Higher Education Mobility Expert. The positions were established for nine-month terms, extendable in line with performance and organizational needs, with applications accepted until 5 February 2026 and detailed qualification requirements set out in dedicated terms of reference.

The significance of this announcement goes beyond staffing. The mandates of the two experts – legal and institutional frameworks on the one hand, and higher education mobility on the other – correspond precisely to the reform agenda that emerged from the 8th TURKUNIB General Assembly in Tashkent in October 2025 and from the Gabala Summit's endorsement of a reorganized Orhun Exchange Programme and a Turkic World Higher Education Area. By building expert capacity within its Secretariat, the OTS laid the groundwork for the decisions subsequently taken by the 9th Meeting of the Ministers of Education in June 2026, including the establishment of a Permanent TURKUNIB Secretariat and a Dedicated Programme Fund for the Orhun Exchange Programme.

For TURKUNIB member universities, this development signals that the mobility and institutional reforms discussed in recent assemblies are moving from concept to implementation – with professional legal, institutional and mobility expertise now dedicated to designing the systems through which students and staff of Turkic world universities will study, teach and conduct research across borders.

headline: Turkic States Adopt Joint Declaration on Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation in Baku
tags: science and technology, innovation, ministerial meeting, Joint Declaration, Action Plan, knowledge economy
paras: The 2nd Ministerial Meeting on Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation of the Organization of Turkic States convened in Baku on 24 October 2025 under the theme “From Strategic Partnership to Technological Integration of the Turkic States.”

Chaired by Minister of Economy of Azerbaijan Mikayil Jabbarov, the meeting brought together Minister of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic Bakyt Sydykov, Minister of Industry and Technology of Türkiye Mehmet Fatih Kacır, Vice-Minister of Industry and Construction of Kazakhstan Rakhymzhan Issakulov, Acting Director of Uzbekistan's Agency for Innovative Development under the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovations Asror Norov, Ambassador of Hungary to Azerbaijan Tamàs Torma, and OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev.

The ministers focused on strengthening cooperation in industry, science, technology and innovation as the foundation of a competitive, knowledge-based and sustainable economic area across the Turkic world. The meeting adopted the Joint Declaration of the 2nd Ministerial Meeting, committing the states to deeper industrial and technological integration, together with an updated Action Plan for 2025–2026 covering the priority areas of cooperation. Kazakhstan will host the 3rd Ministerial Meeting in 2026.

The presence of Uzbekistan's innovation agency – operating under the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation – illustrates how closely this agenda is tied to the university sector: research, technology development and innovation increasingly move through higher education institutions and their partnerships with industry.

For TURKUNIB and its member universities, the Baku Declaration and its accompanying Action Plan define the intergovernmental framework within which joint research programmes, technology transfer and university–industry cooperation across the Turkic states can develop, and signal growing opportunities for universities to contribute to the region's technological integration.

headline: Turkic World Space Cooperation Advances in Tashkent: Joint Satellite Nears Launch as Education and Capacity-Building Take Centre Stage
tags: space cooperation, OTS-SAT, CubeSat, Turkic Space Explorers Academy, STEM, Tashkent
paras: The 5th Meeting of the Heads of Space Agencies of the Organization of Turkic States, held in Tashkent on 30 March 2026 with the participation of OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev, confirmed that space has become one of the most dynamic areas of scientific and technological cooperation in the Turkic world – with education at its core.

The meeting reviewed manufacturing progress and launch preparations for the 12U OTS-SAT Cube Satellite, the flagship joint innovation project of the Turkic states. Days later, the OTS announced that the nanosatellite – designed to support Earth observation, in-orbit technology demonstration and the development of joint space capabilities – had reached its final manufacturing stage and was approaching launch. Participants also worked to finalize the draft Space Industrial Agreement for Capacity Development of Collaboration within the OTS.

Significantly for the academic community, the agenda devoted particular attention to cooperation in education and capacity-building. headline: A Century After the First Baku Turkology Congress, Scholars Gather in Almaty to Chart the Future of Turkic Studies
tags: Turkology, Baku Congress centenary, Turkic Academy, Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, humanities
paras: Marking one hundred years since the First Baku Turkology Congress of 1926, the Turkic Academy and Al-Farabi Kazakh National University convened the International Conference on Turkology, “The Legacy of the First Baku Turkology Congress and the Turkic World in the 21st Century,” in Almaty on 21 May 2026.

Addressing the conference, OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev said that the 1926 congress “laid the intellectual foundations for unity, mutual understanding and closer cooperation among Turkic peoples,” and observed that the intellectual ideas of that gathering have since evolved into today's institutionalized cooperation spanning education, culture, science and youth initiatives. The conference addressed the preservation of the common cultural heritage of the Turkic peoples and initiatives surrounding the Common Turkic Alphabet, with the Secretary General stressing that ongoing cultural and academic initiatives continue to deepen understanding among Turkic societies.

The centenary conference exemplifies the model of cooperation that unites the Turkic world's scientific institutions and its universities: a leading national university, Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, co-organizing a landmark scholarly event with the Turkic Academy, the region's principal research institution.

For TURKUNIB member universities – many of which maintain departments of Turkology, philology and history – the centenary offers both a scholarly milestone and an invitation: the questions first posed in Baku a century ago, from language and alphabet to shared heritage, are today being addressed through the kind of inter-university research collaboration that TURKUNIB exists to foster.

headline: Tashkent International University Assumes the Chairmanship of TURKUNIB for 2025–2026
tags: TURKUNIB chairmanship, Tashkent International University, UNEC, Road Map, Orhun Exchange Programme
paras: The chairmanship of the Turkic Universities Union (TURKUNIB) formally passed to Tashkent International University (TIU) for the 2025–2026 term at a handover ceremony held in Tashkent on 22 January 2025.

Professor Adalat Muradov, Rector of Azerbaijan State University of Economics (UNEC), which concluded its term at the head of the Union, presented a symbolic key to TIU Director Iskandar Yuldashev, marking the transfer of leadership. The ceremony was attended by OTS Deputy Secretary General Dr. Mirvokhid Azimov, Advisor to the Minister of Higher Education, Science and Innovation of Uzbekistan Bobur Rakhimov, and heads and representatives of TURKUNIB member universities.

Speakers emphasized the priorities of the new term: strengthening academic collaboration among member universities, expanding student and faculty exchanges, and developing the Orhun Exchange Programme as the Union's principal mobility instrument. Dr. Azimov and Mr. Yuldashev signed a Road Map setting out the activities planned for the 2025–2026 chairmanship.

The handover set the course for what would become a landmark period in TURKUNIB's development. Under the TIU chairmanship, the Union went on to host its 8th General Assembly in Tashkent in October 2025, admitting 62 new member universities, and to advance the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat and a dedicated fund for the Orhun Exchange Programme – initiatives that took institutional shape over the months that followed.

headline: Institutionalization, Financing and Digitalization: OTS Workshop Examines the Future of the Orhun Process and TURKUNIB
tags: Orhun Process, TURKUNIB, Turkic World Summer School, Ibn Haldun University, institutionalization, digitalization
paras: The structural questions shaping the future of academic mobility in the Turkic world were the focus of a dedicated workshop on the Orhun Process and TURKUNIB, held on 25 June 2025 within the Second Turkic World Summer School hosted by Ibn Haldun University, with the participation of OTS Deputy Secretary General Dr. Mirvokhid Azimov.

The workshop addressed the key challenges confronting the Orhun Exchange Programme and the Turkic Universities Union as they scale up: regulatory alignment among different national higher education systems; the financial frameworks needed to sustain mobility at greater volume; the institutionalization of structures that have until now operated on a rotating, voluntary basis; and the digitalization of processes on which a modern exchange programme depends. Dr. Azimov also delivered an address to the Summer School's participants.

In retrospect, the Istanbul workshop mapped the agenda that would dominate the year that followed. Regulatory alignment, financing, institutionalization and digitalization were precisely the questions taken up by the 8th TURKUNIB General Assembly in Tashkent in October 2025, endorsed at the level of Heads of State in the Gabala Declaration, and carried into implementation through the OTS's recruitment of dedicated experts and the decisions of the 9th Meeting of the Ministers of Education in 2026.

For TURKUNIB member universities, the workshop illustrates how the Union's reform agenda has been built – through sustained expert dialogue linking the OTS Secretariat, universities and young scholars – and signals the practical changes coming to the way inter-university mobility across the Turkic world is organized, funded and administered.

headline: Youth and Sports Ministers of the Turkic States Meet in Tashkent, Set Course for 2026
tags: youth policy, sports, ministerial meeting, Tashkent, World Nomad Games
paras: The 9th Meeting of the Ministers in Charge of Youth and Sports of the Organization of Turkic States convened in Tashkent on 17 October 2025, two days after the same city hosted the 8th General Assembly of the Turkic Universities Union – making it a week in which both the university and youth agendas of the Turkic world converged on the Uzbek capital.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Sports of Uzbekistan Adkham Ikramov and First Deputy Director of Uzbekistan's Agency for Youth Affairs Dilnozaxon Kattaxonova, together with Minister of Youth and Sports of Azerbaijan Farid Gayibov, Minister of Tourism and Sport of Kazakhstan Yerbol Myrzabossynov, Director of the State Agency of Physical Culture and Sports of the Kyrgyz Republic Kazybek Moldazhiyev, Minister of Youth and Sports of Türkiye Osman Aşkın Bak, OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev, and further senior officials from the member and observer states.

Ministers reviewed the youth and sports activities organized under the OTS umbrella during 2025 and discussed concrete projects to promote unity and solidarity among the young people of the Turkic states. The Kyrgyz delegation announced that the 10th Meeting will be held within the framework of the 6th World Nomad Games, scheduled for 31 August – 6 September 2026 in the Kyrgyz Republic.

Youth policy and higher education are closely intertwined: students form a substantial share of the young people these programmes serve, and university campuses are frequent venues for their implementation. The ministerial's outcomes are therefore of practical interest to TURKUNIB member universities engaged in student life, sport and youth development across the Turkic world.

headline: Turkic Academy Marks Fifteen Years of Advancing Shared Scholarship
tags: Turkic Academy, anniversary, research, Common Turkic Alphabet, Vision-2040
paras: The Turkic Academy celebrated its fifteenth anniversary at a ceremony held in Ankara on 18 November 2025, attended by OTS Deputy Secretary General Merey Mukazhan alongside representatives of the sister institutions of the Turkic cooperation family, including TÜRKSOY, TURKPA, the Turkic Culture and Heritage Foundation, the Turkic Investment Fund and the Turkic Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

The programme combined protocol remarks with a presentation, a panel session and an exhibition dedicated to the Academy's work. In his address, Deputy Secretary General Mukazhan highlighted the Academy's fifteen years of advancing research on the shared history, language and cultural heritage of the Turkic world, and emphasized education and scientific cooperation as core elements of the “Turkic World Vision-2040.” He also welcomed the adoption of the Common Turkic Alphabet as a development strengthening mutual understanding and cultural unity across the region.

Since its establishment, the Turkic Academy has grown into the principal scientific institution of the Turkic cooperation framework – coordinating joint research projects, publications and scholarly gatherings that draw on the expertise of universities throughout the member states, from the “Common History of Turkic Countries” project to the centenary conference on Turkology co-organized with Al-Farabi Kazakh National University in 2026.

For TURKUNIB member universities, the Academy is a natural institutional partner: its research agenda in history, linguistics and heritage runs through university departments across the Turkic world, and its anniversary is a reminder of how far the region's shared scientific infrastructure has developed in a decade and a half.

headline: Tashkent Forum Celebrates UNESCO's Proclamation of World Turkic Language Family Day
tags: World Turkic Language Family Day, UNESCO, youth education forum, International Turkic States University, Tashkent
paras: The Turkic World Youth Education Forum, dedicated to the first observance of World Turkic Language Family Day, was held in Tashkent on 15 December 2025, organized by the International Turkic States University. More than 150 participants – government representatives, academics, think-tank experts, diplomats and young people – took part.

The forum marked a historic milestone: the official proclamation of 15 December as World Turkic Language Family Day at the 43rd session of the UNESCO General Conference in November 2025, an international recognition of the linguistic and cultural heritage shared by the Turkic peoples.

Discussions unfolded in two panel sessions: “Sustainable Development and Strategic Cooperation of the Turkic States in a Changing Geopolitical Environment” and “Toward Turkic Cultural Identity and a Common Spiritual Space: The Role of Turkic World Youth in the Process of Integration.” Addressing the forum, OTS Deputy Secretary General Dr. Mirvokhid Azimov emphasized education and youth as a top priority within the OTS's more than thirty areas of cooperation, and recalled the Charter of the Turkic World adopted at the 2024 Bishkek Summit.

That a university convened the forum is itself telling: higher education institutions are increasingly the venues where the Turkic world's cultural, linguistic and youth agendas meet. For TURKUNIB member universities – many of which teach and research Turkic languages – the UNESCO recognition offers an annual occasion to showcase their scholarship and connect their students to a shared regional heritage.

headline: Oriental Studies and the Orhun Programme: OTS Secretary General Visits Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies
tags: Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, Orhun Exchange Programme, academic partnership, lecture, Tashkent
paras: OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev visited Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies (TSUOS) on 13 November 2025, meeting Rector Gulchehra Rixsiyeva to discuss the expansion of educational cooperation and academic partnerships among the Turkic countries.

The two sides agreed to strengthen collaboration and increase joint initiatives through the Orhun Exchange Programme of the Turkic Universities Union – a concrete, university-level commitment to the mobility instrument at the heart of TURKUNIB's agenda. During the visit, the Secretary General also delivered a lecture entitled “Current State and Prospects for the Development of Cooperation within the Framework of the OTS,” emphasizing to students and faculty the role of educational and cultural cooperation in deepening ties among the member states.

The visit continued an engagement begun earlier in the year, when the TSUOS leadership visited OTS Headquarters in Istanbul in April 2025, and formed part of a series of university visits by the Secretary General in Tashkent that week, including Tashkent International University – TURKUNIB's Chair University – and Nordic International University, one of the Union's newest members.

Agreements of this kind show the Orhun Exchange Programme working as intended: not an abstract framework, but a channel through which individual universities commit to concrete joint activity. For the wider TURKUNIB membership, TSUOS's engagement illustrates how universities can anchor their internationalization strategies in the Union's common mobility architecture.

headline: Manas University at Thirty: A Flagship of Joint Higher Education in the Turkic World
tags: Manas University, anniversary, joint university, Kyrgyz Republic, TURKUNIB
paras: OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev paid a working visit to Kyrgyz-Turkish Manas University on 19 September 2025 at the university's invitation, joining the institution's leadership as it marked thirty years since its foundation.

The Secretary General met Rector Prof. Dr. Alpaslan Ceylan, Deputy Rector Prof. Dr. Almaz Ibraev and members of the faculty, acknowledging the university's accomplishments over three decades. The visit placed particular emphasis on expanding cooperation through the Turkic Universities Union (TURKUNIB), of which Manas University is a member. The Secretary General also gave an interview to the university's television channel on the structure, tasks and objectives of the Organization of Turkic States, and was presented with the commemorative medal “30 Years of Manas University.”

Established jointly by the Kyrgyz Republic and Türkiye, Manas University stands among the earliest and most successful experiments in shared higher education in the Turkic world – a bi-national institution educating students from across the region decades before a Turkic World Higher Education Area became a formal policy objective.

As the Turkic states now work to institutionalize mobility, quality assurance and diploma recognition across their university systems, the experience accumulated by joint institutions such as Manas University is a valuable resource for the entire TURKUNIB membership – living proof that deeply integrated, cross-border higher education in the Turkic world can flourish.

headline: OTS Engages OECD Skills Agenda at Istanbul Summit on Talent and Lifelong Learning
tags: OECD, Skills Summit, human capital, lifelong learning, Istanbul
paras: OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev participated in the OECD Skills Summit 2026, held in Istanbul on 27–28 April 2026 under the theme “Unlocking Talent Across Generations.”

The summit's opening was addressed by President of Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Minister of Labour and Social Security of Türkiye Prof. Dr. Vedat Işıkhan and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann. Discussions ranged across skills development, human capital enhancement, inclusive labour markets, lifelong learning, vocational training and innovation-driven growth. The OTS Secretary General attended the official opening ceremony, took part in the tour-de-table session on skills policy development, exchanged views with the OECD Secretary-General, and presented the OTS's institutional framework in the fields of labour, employment and social protection.

The Organization's presence at a flagship OECD event reflects the growing international engagement of the Turkic cooperation framework on education-adjacent policy. Skills and human capital sit immediately downstream of higher education: the questions debated in Istanbul – how societies develop talent, retrain workforces and sustain lifelong learning – are questions in which universities are principal actors.

For TURKUNIB member universities, the OTS's engagement with the OECD skills agenda signals opportunities to align regional academic cooperation with international best practice in skills and employability – dimensions increasingly important to graduates navigating the labour markets of the Turkic states and beyond.

headline: Hungary and the Turkic States Convene Summit on Culture, Education and Innovation in Budapest
tags: Hungary, Budapest, education, innovation, culture, observer state
paras: The Hungarian-Turkic Summit on Culture, Education and Innovation opened in Budapest on 28 April 2025, bringing together ministers and high-level officials from Hungary and the Turkic states around three fields central to the region's long-term development.

Addressing the opening, OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev emphasized Hungary's role as an Observer of the Organization of Turkic States and highlighted the dynamic, multifaceted cooperation that has developed between Hungary and the Turkic states. He underlined the significance of convening ministers and senior officials specifically on culture, education and innovation – domains in which Hungary's engagement with the Turkic world has been especially active, notably through the scholarship opportunities Hungarian institutions extend to students from the region.

The Budapest summit acquires added meaning in light of subsequent developments. At the 8th General Assembly of the Turkic Universities Union in Tashkent in October 2025, the Government of Hungary presented proposals for a joint Research, Development and Innovation Fund and for an enhanced Orhun Exchange Programme – initiatives consistent with the education-and-innovation agenda convened in Budapest months earlier.

For TURKUNIB and its member universities, Hungary's sustained engagement widens the Union's horizons: an observer state with strong European academic networks actively proposing instruments for research funding and student mobility strengthens the bridge between the Turkic higher education space and the wider European academic community.

headline: Young Delegates Simulate Turkic Cooperation at Model OTS 2026 in Azerbaijan

paras: The international youth camp “Model Organization of Turkic States 2026” was held in Quba, Azerbaijan, from 25 to 30 May 2026, organized by Azerbaijan's Ministry of Youth and Sports and Ministry of Justice together with the Justice Volunteers Public Union, with the OTS Secretariat represented by its Director for Projects, Murodjon Mustofoev.

The programme combined panel discussions on youth innovation, governance and international negotiation with expert meetings, training sessions and the drafting of memoranda under institutional guidance, alongside cultural exhibitions, concerts and team-building activities. Senior Azerbaijani officials, including Deputy Minister of Youth and Sports Indira Hajiyeva, took part.

As its concluding outcome, participants jointly drafted and adopted a memorandum recommending enhanced cooperation in youth policy, education, law, digital transformation, culture and media – a youth-authored articulation of priorities that closely mirrors the formal agenda of the Turkic states.

Simulation formats of this kind cultivate precisely the skills universities seek to develop – negotiation, policy analysis, public speaking and cross-cultural collaboration. headline: New TURKUNIB Member in Focus: OTS Secretary General Visits Nordic International University in Tashkent
tags: Nordic International University, new member, TURKUNIB, Orhun Exchange Programme, Tashkent
paras: OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev visited Nordic International University (NIU) in Tashkent on 15 November 2025, at the initiative of the university's leadership, meeting Chairman of the Supervisory Board Alisher Jurayev and Rector Dr. Sherzod Mustafaqulov.

The Secretary General congratulated NIU on its admission to the Turkic Universities Union – the university joined TURKUNIB during the 8th General Assembly held in Tashkent on 15 October 2025, one of the 62 institutions admitted in the Union's largest-ever enlargement. He encouraged the university to cooperate closely with Tashkent International University, which holds the TURKUNIB chairmanship for 2025–2026.

The two sides discussed expanding educational cooperation and agreed to implement joint projects within the framework of TURKUNIB's Orhun Exchange Programme. The university's leadership also presented several of NIU's ongoing projects to the Secretary General.

The visit illustrates what TURKUNIB's enlargement means in practice: within a month of admission, a new member university was engaging directly with the OTS leadership and committing to joint activity under the Union's mobility programme. For the dozens of institutions that joined TURKUNIB in 2025, NIU's early engagement offers a template for translating membership into concrete cooperation.

headline: From the Turkic World to Silicon Valley: OTS Deepens Innovation-Ecosystem Ties with Silk Road Innovation Hub
tags: Silk Road Innovation Hub, Silicon Valley, startups, innovation ecosystem, acceleration
paras: During a visit to the United States, OTS Secretary General Ambassador Kubanychbek Omuraliev visited the Silk Road Innovation Hub in California on 20 December 2025, meeting its Founder and Chief Executive Officer Aset Abdualiyev.

The Secretary General was briefed on the Hub's activities – startup acceleration, innovation support and ecosystem building connecting entrepreneurs from Central Asia and the wider region with Silicon Valley – as well as its medium- and long-term development strategies. The visit built on an existing relationship: in July 2025, the OTS Secretariat and the Silk Road Innovation Hub had launched joint startup initiatives aimed at supporting entrepreneurs from the Turkic states.

The Organization's cultivation of ties with one of the world's leading innovation ecosystems reflects a broader ambition running through the Turkic cooperation agenda – visible equally in the Baku ministerial on science, technology and innovation, the AI theme of the 2026 Turkistan Summit, and the joint satellite programme: connecting the region's emerging technology sector to global networks of capital, expertise and markets.

Universities are foundational to that ambition. Student startups, university incubators and technology transfer offices are where much of the Turkic world's entrepreneurial talent first takes shape, and bridges to Silicon Valley of the kind the OTS is building expand the horizons available to the innovators emerging from TURKUNIB member universities.
